bug_semantics: LimitToString tracked only one ObjectToString conversion: every top-level expression reset _currentToStringLength to zero, while TemplateContext.Write forwarded each converted string to StringBuilderOutput, whose Builder.Append calls imposed no render-wide bound. A template could therefore build a 1,048,575-character string, emit it in each of 1,000 default-limited loop iterations, pass the 1 MiB per-call check every time, and accumulate roughly 1 GiB until the host exhausted memory.
flaw_origin: Commit b858377886c35bfedb2768de9b057377909c2e95 introduced LimitToString, _currentToStringLength, and the top-level reset in ObjectToString, but did not connect that accounting to cumulative TemplateContext output. The older unconditional StringBuilderOutput append was the allocation sink, not the commit that created the advisory-specific LimitToString bypass. Commit b5ac4bf30459fdc76964e3f751e16f7e96079ea7 later changed LimitToString's default from 0 to 1,048,576 for release 6.6.0 without creating the flawed counter lifetime. Commit 98563216488161a9edeba6c37c7cf82c98319c9b fixed the lifecycle by accounting every synchronous and asynchronous output chunk against one render-wide counter and resetting that counter only with TemplateContext.Reset.
ai_marker: absent: the raw commit object for b858377886c35bfedb2768de9b057377909c2e95 names Alexandre Mutel <alexandre_mutel@live.com> as both author and committer and contains only the subject 'Add TemplateContext.LimitToString'; it has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI-attribution trailer.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/scriban/scriban/security/advisories/GHSA-m2p3-hwv5-xpqw identifies src/Scriban/TemplateContext.Helpers.cs ObjectToString's per-top-level-call reset, src/Scriban/TemplateContext.cs Write(SourceSpan, object), and src/Scriban/Runtime/StringBuilderOutput.cs unconditional append; it specifies affected <=6.6.0, patched 7.0.0, and the repeated near-1-MiB-string PoC.

git log -L '/public virtual string ObjectToString/',+35:src/Scriban/TemplateContext.Helpers.cs 98563216488161a9edeba6c37c7cf82c98319c9b^ follows the surviving reset backward through later edits and reaches b858377886c35bfedb2768de9b057377909c2e95 as the commit that added the if (_objectToStringLevel == 0) { _currentToStringLength = 0; } block and LimitToString checks.

git show b858377886c35bfedb2768de9b057377909c2e95 shows a focused two-file change adding LimitToString and the flawed counter lifetime; git grep -n -E '_currentToStringLength|LimitToString' d4d64f8f15df9683ec0d51d4906edc4b3cef5ff5 -- src/Scriban/TemplateContext.Helpers.cs src/Scriban/TemplateContext.cs returns no matches, directly verifying absence in the immediate parent tree.

git grep at b858377886c35bfedb2768de9b057377909c2e95 finds _currentToStringLength at TemplateContext.Helpers.cs:74, its reset at :87, the per-object checks beginning at :93, and LimitToString's initialization/property at TemplateContext.cs:118 and :193. git blame 6.6.0 -L 89,96 attributes the still-present reset at release line 93 to b858377886c35bfedb2768de9b057377909c2e95.

git log -S 'Builder.Append(text, offset, count)' traces the pre-existing output sink to bfa7fc100ca6d337bd61247319080f91767f462a; git grep at tag 6.6.0 confirms unconditional appends at StringBuilderOutput.cs:49 and :70 alongside the b858 reset at TemplateContext.Helpers.cs:93. This older sink is necessary context, but b858 is the smallest commit that first created the claimed limit-and-bypass mechanism.

git show b5ac4bf30459fdc76964e3f751e16f7e96079ea7 shows only the later default change LimitToString = 0 to 1048576 in TemplateContext.cs (plus unrelated parser-limit edits), so it exposed the existing b858 flaw under default settings rather than writing the flawed mechanism.

git diff 98563216488161a9edeba6c37c7cf82c98319c9b^ 98563216488161a9edeba6c37c7cf82c98319c9b shows _currentOutputLength, GetAllowedOutputCount, WriteOutputChunk/WriteOutputChunkAsync, ellipsis handling, replacement of direct Output.Write calls, and ResetOutputLimitTracking; this is the direct causal fix in both synchronous and asynchronous render paths: https://github.com/scriban/scriban/commit/98563216488161a9edeba6c37c7cf82c98319c9b.

Release-boundary checks resolve 6.6.0 to b5ac4bf30459fdc76964e3f751e16f7e96079ea7 and 7.0.0 to 25d148a104dd4d679a1a1932442616599e003c2f. git tag --contains b858377886c35bfedb2768de9b057377909c2e95 includes 3.0.0 through 6.6.0; git tag --contains 98563216488161a9edeba6c37c7cf82c98319c9b starts at 7.0.0. merge-base(fix, 6.6.0) is b5ac4bf30459fdc76964e3f751e16f7e96079ea7, while merge-base(fix, 7.0.0) is the fix itself, proving the advertised unpatched/patched boundary.

reasoning: The advisory's security contract is not merely that StringBuilder can grow; it is that LimitToString purports to constrain conversion but can be restarted for every rendered expression. History separates three lifecycle points. The output sink predates the control. b858377886c35bfedb2768de9b057377909c2e95 is the smallest real BIC because it first added both the LimitToString contract and the reset that confines accounting to one ObjectToString call; its immediate parent has neither symbol, and -L history confirms later edits preserved that reset rather than reintroducing it. b5ac4bf30459fdc76964e3f751e16f7e96079ea7 only enabled the already-flawed control by default in 6.6.0. The direct fix 98563216488161a9edeba6c37c7cf82c98319c9b moved enforcement to cumulative output chunks and is contained first in 7.0.0. Although versions before the b858-bearing 3.0 line had generally unbounded output, the specific LimitToString bypass begins at b858; that distinction avoids mislabeling either the legacy writer or the later default-value change as the BIC. Finally, the b858 commit object has no AI authorship signal, so later or fix-side attribution cannot change the BIC-only NOT_AI verdict.
